## About Me

:::: {style="display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 30px; margin-bottom: 30px;"}
<img src="images/me3.jpg" alt="Rabea Hinsching" style="width:280px; border-radius:12px;"/>
  
<div>

I am a PhD candidate in Economics at the University of East Anglia. My research is in applied microeconomics, with a focus on development, natural resources, and political economy. I am particularly interested in how firms, governments, and local institutions shape development outcomes, and how these processes affect communities. 

<!--My work is also informed by perspectives from sociology and political economy, especially in understanding the role of local institutions, narratives, and power structures.-->

My job market paper examines the developmental impact of mining companies’ social investments in South Africa’s Gauteng Province. You can find the latest draft <a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Su8FBmJKlBsRZP-Xc4hiRn4sGrQ9kLhz/view?usp=sharing" target="_blank">here</a>.

As part of my research, I collected data on mining companies' social investments from corporate reports using a GPT-based algorithm. The code for the project is available on my <a href="https://github.com/rabeahinsching/CSI_Database" target="_blank">GitHub</a>. I am currently developing this dataset into a publicly accessible project tracker. An early version is available on this website under “CSI Tracker”.
